title: Bridges between words
prompt:
One word fills all three gaps. Each gap needs a word that ends the word on its left and starts the word on its right, making two compound words each time.

- SUN ____ HOUSE
- MOON ____ YEAR
- FLASH ____ BULB

What is the word?
hints: Which of the three lines gives you the most to go on?
Which word can follow FLASH to make a common compound, and can that same word also come before BULB?
Does your word from the FLASH line also fit after SUN and MOON, and before HOUSE and YEAR?
solution:
**Light**: sunlight and lighthouse, moonlight and light-year, flashlight and lightbulb.

A good way in is to notice what the left-hand words share. The sun, the moon and a flash all give off something, and that same word also starts *house*, *year* and *bulb*. Each line has to work in both directions, so checking all six compounds confirms the answer.
